quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who should go first?

options.text: The driver on your left.
The driver who got there first.
The driver across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who got there first.
questions.explanation: Drivers go through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. If two cars arrive at the same time, the car on the left must let the car on the right go first.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
Drink caffeine.
Roll down the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Take breaks every hour on long trips to avoid tired driving. If possible, take turns driving with another person so you can both rest.

questions.question: If your car's rear end skids to the left, which way should you steer?

options.text: Steer right.
Steer left.
Tap the brakes lightly and shift to neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This straightens out your car.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the side with the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from the side with the broken line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid line and a broken line together, you can only pass from the side with the broken line. You cannot pass from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Slow down and yield to other traffic.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians go, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: No one can pass.
Both lanes can pass.
The right lane can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. No one can pass when you see double solid yellow lines.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before the turn is complete.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is unsafe to turn off a signal before the turn is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians what you are going to do.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation?

options.text: Be aware of everything around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be aware of everything around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always watch what is happening around your vehicle. Check the front, sides, and rear to spot problems early so you can change speed or position safely.

questions.question: What does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: No one can pass.
Both directions can pass.
Only the side with the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only the side with the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When there is a dashed line and a solid line together, only the traffic next to the dashed line can pass. Traffic next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: When do large trucks usually lose speed?

options.text: Going up long or steep hills.
Going around long, gradual curves.
Going down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Going up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller cars. They often lose speed going up long or steep hills. Give trucks extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: You see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Move right and go around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk. Wait until they finish crossing before you drive.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
Slow down and use high beam headlights.
Flash your lights to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows before driving. Remove snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An octagon sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop where you can see traffic.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to where you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Drive at normal speed.
Brake hard as soon as you start to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose contact with the road in wet conditions. The best way to prevent this is to drive slowly in rain.

questions.question: A car with bright headlights is coming toward you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other car passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look at bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Winding road
Loose gravel
Slippery when wet

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet. Drive carefully.

questions.question: You park uphill where there is no curb. After setting the parking brake, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. This keeps your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear going down a steep hill.
Speed up for curves and slow down to exit.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. You do not know what is ahead. Braking on a curve can cause skidding.

questions.question: What does a "No passing zone" sign tell drivers?

options.text: Speed up a little.
It is not safe to pass other vehicles.
Keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass other vehicles in that area. The road ahead likely has poor visibility, making it unsafe to pass.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up the radio volume.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: If you struggle to keep your eyes open, drift out of your lane, or need to turn up the radio to stay awake, you are too tired to drive safely. Park in a safe place and rest.

questions.question: How can you avoid being an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Follow the car in front of you very closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Focus on driving and do not get upset by other drivers. Allow extra time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers on the road.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, you should drive at:

options.text: About the same speed as freeway traffic.
The posted speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: About the same speed as freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels so your vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is always safe.
Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
How fast you drive does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because it frustrates other drivers and may cause them to pass unsafely. Drive with traffic, within the speed limit.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is crossing the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is there.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes must always have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and reduces its effects.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Even with proper mirrors, all vehicles have blind spots. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address attached to that vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are entering.
Truck exit only.
A steep downgrade is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep downgrade is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will go steeply downward. Check your brakes.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers pull behind large vehicles before passing them.
Because following too closely traps you in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: The driver of a large vehicle cannot see you if you are directly behind them. Stay farther back so you can see around the vehicle and see the road ahead.

questions.question: If you must park where parking is not usually allowed, what should you do?

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure your vehicle is visible from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle is visible from all directions.
questions.explanation: Your parked vehicle should not be a hazard. Make sure drivers approaching from any direction can see your car.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk and keep your speed the same.
Speed up to get past them quickly.
Slow down and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass carefully.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What should you do before backing your vehicle?

options.text: Walk around the vehicle to check that no people or objects are behind it.
Rev your engine.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the vehicle to check that no people or objects are behind it.
questions.explanation: Always walk around your vehicle before backing. Look over your shoulder and through the rear window. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When parking downhill, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Toward the curb or side of the road.
Away from the curb or side of the road.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the curb or side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road. This prevents your car from rolling into traffic.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop completely at the intersection.
Drive at your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and proceed with caution. Slow down as you approach it.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle in front moves right to let you pass.
When the yellow line on your side is broken.
When the yellow line on the opposite side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Even small amounts of alcohol can affect how well you judge situations and control your body. Driving after drinking any amount of alcohol is dangerous and illegal.

questions.question: You are in the left of two lanes going your direction, and many vehicles are passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane to keep traffic flowing.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to pass or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than traffic around you, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual things on the road:

options.text: Creates traffic jams.
Stops rear-end crashes.
Helps traffic move faster by preventing crashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Creates traffic jams.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at accidents or unusual things. This is called rubbernecking. It causes traffic jams and makes congestion worse.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing down is always a yield sign. When you see this sign, be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must turn right.
No right turns allowed.
You can turn right when the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. It is against the law to turn right at any place where this sign is posted.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic rules. You must follow them. This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for possible dangers. This sign tells you that pedestrians may be crossing the road ahead. Watch for people crossing.

questions.question: A distraction while driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve or change direction.
Anything that takes your focus away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your focus away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. Distracted driving can cause crashes, injuries, and deaths.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look straight at the headlights of cars coming toward you.
Stay farther back from the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder than daytime driving because you cannot see as well. It is harder to judge speed and distance. Stay farther back from the car ahead of you. This gives you more time to stop if they stop suddenly. Use your headlights correctly at night.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on your hazard lights.
Turn on your hazard lights and drive off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard lights and drive off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, turn on your emergency flashers so other drivers can see you. Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic as soon as possible.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Before you start the engine.
Anytime you need to use them.
Before you get in the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Your safety and others' safety depends on what you do before driving. Before you move your vehicle, adjust your seat, adjust your mirrors, fasten your seatbelt, and secure loose items. Never adjust your mirrors while the car is moving.

questions.question: When pulling into traffic from a parked spot, you:

options.text: Should drive slower than other cars for 200 feet.
Should wait for enough space to match the speed of traffic.
Should wait for two cars to pass, then enter the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wait for enough space to match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When you merge into traffic in the city or on the highway, wait for enough space to get your car up to the same speed as the other cars around you.
